key_insight: The paper introduces a fully unsupervised, multi-round self-learning framework that uses graph neural networks to iteratively cluster node-attributed graphs while refining the graph representation each round.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical approach for clustering real-world networks where both connectivity and node attributes matter, improving robustness when either signal alone is weak.
method: GNN learns node embeddings from the original graph plus a context graph.
Embeddings are clustered, and the resulting clusters are used to update the graph for the next round.
Multiple self-learning rounds replace a single long training pass and improve clustering quality.
evidence_signal: Abstract reports that the method outperforms network-only or attribute-only baselines on synthetic data, and is competitive with state-of-the-art methods on real datasets when cluster sizes are balanced.
watch_item: Performance may depend on balanced cluster sizes, so results may be less reliable for highly imbalanced real-world graphs.
paper_title: Clustering Node Attributed Networks with Graph Neural Networks and Self Learning
